analysis:
Examined docs/developer/test.md (test documentation only, no executable change), scripts/ci-component-paths.py, scripts/install-release-cmake.sh and scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py. These are CI routing and build-tooling changes, not provider runtime code. They do not touch the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket (TB-002), key custody (A-002, A-003), attestation (TB-009), App Attest (TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041) or the add-on boundaries (TB-012, TB-013).

ci-component-paths.py adds a `mimo_audio` component and a MIMO_AUDIO pattern list. It only gates whether a CI job runs the MiMo audio gate and downloads the 1.87 GB codec. Default-branch pushes and COMMON-file changes still select every component (`full` and `dict.fromkeys`), so the gate cannot be skipped on master. A PR touching only unlisted inputs skips the audio gate, which is a coverage tradeoff, not a security regression. The test file cross-checks that every MIMO_AUDIO input is also a provider input, which keeps provider lanes selected.

install-release-cmake.sh now prefers a CMake copy from `$RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE/cmake/3.31.12/universal` when a `.complete` marker exists and the binary reports the exact version. Otherwise it falls back to the sha256-verified download. The cached path skips the checksum check and trusts the runner image's tool cache plus a version-string check, so a compromised runner image or cache could supply a trojaned cmake for release Metal builds. That is a supply-chain trust assumption on CI-runner image integrity. The supplied evidence does not show that the tool cache is writable by untrusted parties; the threat model puts the backend and CI infrastructure out of scope and the provider artifact build is only partially in scope. I record this as an unverified contract, not a finding. Reviewers should confirm that the release-signing build runs only on trusted images, or that the cache is root-owned. The `-f` and version check run before use, and `RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE` defaults to a nonexistent path, so it fails closed to the download.

No findings.
